data.body: `role-to-assume` is resolved dynamically via `secrets[matrix.role_secret]` for the `china` and `govcloud` matrix entries (`LAYER_PUBLISH_ROLE_ARN_CN`, `LAYER_PUBLISH_ROLE_ARN_GOV`), but nothing validates these secrets are actually configured before this step runs. If `LAYER_PUBLISH_REGIONS` (or the `regions` dispatch input) is later extended to include a `cn-*` or `us-gov-*` region without also adding the matching secret to the `lambda-layer-publish` environment, `role-to-assume` resolves to an empty string and `configure-aws-credentials` fails with an opaque OIDC/assume-role error instead of a clear message pointing at the missing secret — and the PR description only calls out configuring `LAYER_PUBLISH_ROLE_ARN`, making this easy to hit unknowingly. Add a guard (e.g. in the preceding region-selection step) that fails fast with an explicit message such as 'LAYER_PUBLISH_ROLE_ARN_CN must be set to publish to configured China regions' whenever `steps.regions.outputs.regions` is non-empty but the corresponding matrix secret is empty, and document all three required secrets alongside `LAYER_PUBLISH_ROLE_ARN`.
